title: The King Above the Roaring Sea
overview: This short song celebrates the LORD as king over the whole world, steadier and stronger than the wild sea that threatens it.

parts.label: The LORD is king (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: God is pictured dressed as a ruler, in royal robes for honor and with strength wrapped around him like a soldier's belt. Because he rules, the world stands firm, and his throne is older than anything else that exists.

parts.label: Louder than the waves (vv. 3-4)
parts.note: In the ancient world the raging sea stood for chaos and danger, so the poem lets the waves roar and then places the LORD above them, stronger still. Many readers also take the floods as a picture of hostile nations or of life's upheavals, though that is an interpretation.

parts.label: Reliable decrees, holy house (v. 5)
parts.note: God's decrees are called completely reliable, as steady as his rule over the sea. Holiness, meaning being set apart for God, is said to suit his "house" forever; the psalm does not say exactly what that house is, and it is often taken as the temple, while Christians have also read it as God's people.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether "the LORD reigns" mainly describes God's rule over the world right now or looks ahead to a fuller kingdom still to come, and many hold both together.
think: When life feels like rough, rising water, what, if anything, has ever felt steady enough to hold on to?
